1.why: `/api/reset-validate` and `/api/password-update` compare the submitted token strictly against `session.resetToken` (only set when the request matched MOCK_ACCOUNT_EMAIL), so a code only works within the session/account it was issued for, though there is no real per-user record.

2.why: Reset tokens are stored solely in the server-side session and validated with `token === session.resetToken`, so a code from one session/user cannot be used in another — the statement is false of this system.

3.why: Nothing in `/api/password-update` rotates the session id or deletes other sessions, so any pre-existing session cookies remain valid until the 30-minute TTL expires.

4.why: `Bun.serve` is configured with TLS cert/key, HTTP-only port 3001 returns 426, HSTS is set and non-HTTPS requests are rejected (421), but no explicit minimum TLS version is pinned, relying on Bun defaults.

5.why: Passwords are hashed with bcrypt cost 12 and traffic is TLS-protected, but reset tokens are kept in memory in cleartext (not hashed) and returned verbatim to the client as `mockDeliveryToken`.

6.why: There is no email message at all — 'delivery' is simulated by returning the reset code in the API JSON and printing it to the page log/console, which does not guard the secret.

7.why: Inputs are type-checked, trimmed, length-limited (4KB body, maxLength fields), validated with regexes for email/code/password, and all UI is rendered via `textContent`/`setAttribute` with a nonce-based CSP.

8.why: The application performs no redirects or outbound requests; navigation is limited to an allow-list of internal screen names, with `form-action 'self'`, `base-uri 'none'` and `default-src 'none'`.

9.why: No email templates exist, and the equivalent notification content is generated with DOM text nodes only, so no user input is ever interpolated into HTML or script.

10.why: Server error responses are generic with no stack traces, but the reset token and MFA code are deliberately written to `console.log` and the visible 'Logs' pane, so secrets do appear in logs.

11.why: Passwords are bcrypt-hashed, but the MFA secret is hardcoded in the source (`const MFA_CODE = "482913"`) along with the account email constant.

12.why: The static, hardcoded six-digit MFA code `482913` functions as a default credential that always satisfies `/api/mfa-verify`, and the mock account email is fixed in code.

13.why: `rateAllowed` throttles reset requests (3/15 min), reset-code guesses (5/15 min) and MFA attempts (5/15 min), though counters are per-session and can be reset by obtaining a fresh cookie via `/api/bootstrap`.

14.why: `/api/reset-request` returns the identical generic message and an opaque random token for every valid-format email, so the immediate response does not disclose account existence (only later validation failure differs).

15.why: Tokens come from `crypto.getRandomValues` over 32 bytes encoded base64url, are bound to the session, single-use (`resetUsed`) and expire after 15 minutes.
